did: As SLOW-PROBE, I investigated why everything on home is slow: our code or the hardware. I named sixteen code choices that cost time, fixed a falsifiable rule before measuring, timed whisper, Kokoro and the render's scene encodes on a cloud bench for free, and read three rounds of the owner's readings from home. By the rule the code is to blame: home sat idle 81% of the watched time, renders could not start for memory 37% of it, and transcription and speech each waste 2× or more. For a running render, though, home's N100 core is 5 to 7 times slower than a server core, so the hardware is the bigger single factor there, with a free 1.7× from code first. I sent the evidence in four versions to SLOW-MAKE, retracting in v3 a busy share that had counted missing monitoring data as busy, and filed issue 3540 with the free changes and whose call each is.

calls.title: How to time a render without a full essay
options: Build a valid cards essay and run the whole recorder
Time the render's heaviest steps alone: speech and a scene encode
calls.why: A full run needs a valid essay, the stage and a browser per card, and the two heavy steps carry most of the time; home's own render times then checked the estimate.
calls.undo: Run a full cards essay through the recorder on the bench and compare its time with the estimate.

calls.title: Whether to file the owner's three asks or list them
options: File each ask as its own issue now
List them in issue 3540 for the coordinator to file
calls.why: The coordinator offered either, and the server issues they gate are also the coordinator's to file.
calls.undo: File asks A, B and C from issue 3540 as their own issues.

left: How many cores a render really uses: no render was running to measure, and two CPU counters on home disagree by 2.4 to 4.3 times.
The transcriber's per-take timings on home: no attempt lines were found in 14 days of its logs.
Three asks (A, B, C in issue 3540) and the server issues for the free changes, which this session could not file on server.
